channel.title: NewsCenter — Top 5 news of the day — 2026-11-09
channel.description: The five news that matter most today, chosen from Laurent's newsletters. 88 news received.

item.title: 1. OpenAI raises $11 billion, while Anthropic prepares to go public
item.description: Why it matters: OpenAI’s $11 billion financing and Anthropic’s planned IPO underscore the extraordinary capital demands and increasingly concentrated market power of frontier AI. OpenAI raised approximately $11 billion at a valuation of $1.25 trillion, below its initial targets. Anthropic, meanwhile, is preparing a Nasdaq listing at an estimated valuation of around $1.5 trillion.

item.title: 2. Nvidia investigates possible espionage operation targeting Jensen Huang
item.description: Why it matters: A possible foreign intelligence operation targeting Nvidia’s CEO could affect leadership, security, investor confidence, and the broader AI supply chain. Nvidia’s board of directors is investigating whether its CEO Jensen Huang was the target of a foreign intelligence operation. The matter could have major repercussions for Nvidia and the artificial intelligence sector.

item.title: 3. Coding agents fail at nearly three out of four real-world tasks
item.description: Why it matters: Real-world benchmark results showing coding agents solve only about one in four tasks challenge inflated capability claims and highlight the gap between demos and dependable enterprise automation. Alibaba’s Co-Design Bench benchmark, based on real user requests, shows that GPT-6 Astra fully solves only 26.4% of tasks. Yet the same models score more than 99% on older benchmarks.

item.title: 4. American voters reject data center projects
item.description: Why it matters: Voter rejection of data-center projects signals growing political resistance to the infrastructure needed for AI expansion and raises costs and permitting risks. In Alhambra, California, 83% of voters supported banning data centers, while in Wells, Maine, 82% approved a 180-day pause. OpenAI now proposes paying for electricity and infrastructure, publishing more information, and investing locally to win residents’ support.

item.title: 5. U.S. AI safety testing center informally reports to the White House
item.description: Why it matters: The U.S. AI safety testing center’s informal reporting relationship with the White House suggests tighter political oversight of AI evaluation despite unresolved governance gaps. The U.S. government center responsible for testing AI safety has begun informally reporting to a White House office. It still has no permanent director.
